item.title: Fixing Matplotlib Subplot Overlap: Effective Spacing Techniques
item.description:
“Fixing Matplotlib Subplot Overlap: Effective Spacing Techniques”

Techniques for Adjusting Matplotlib Subplot Spacing

Here are several accepted and practical approaches to mitigate subplot overlap in Matplotlib figures:

Method 1: Utilizing tight_layout()

The matplotlib.pyplot.tight_layout() function or the figure method fig.tight_layout() automatically adjusts subplot parameters to give a tight layout. This is often the first and simplest solution to attempt.

Practical Implementation Example:

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Creating a grid of 4x4 subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(nrows=4, ncols=4, figsize=(8, 8))

# Apply tight_layout either to the figure or pyplot interface
fig.tight_layout() 
# Alternatively: plt.tight_layout()

plt.show()

This function dynamically calculates the necessary padding to fit all elements neatly within the figure boundary, preventing overlaps.

item.title: Solved: How to Fix ValueError Unknown Projection '3d' in Matplotlib
item.description:
Question:

Encountering the error ValueError: Unknown projection ‘3d’ can be frustrating, especially when attempting to run example scripts from Matplotlib after a fresh installation. Below is an example script where users frequently get stuck.

from mpl_toolkits.mplot3d import axes3d
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig = plt.figure()
ax = fig.gca(projection='3d')
X, Y, Z = axes3d.get_test_data(0.05)
cset = ax.contour(X, Y, Z, 16, extend3d=True)
ax.clabel(cset, fontsize=9, inline=1)

plt.show()

The above code can lead to the following traceback:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  raise ValueError("Unknown projection '%s'" % projection)
ValueError: Unknown projection '3d'

Solutions:

Solution 1: Update or Verify Matplotlib Version

The primary reason for the ValueError: Unknown projection ‘3d’ is typically related to the version of Matplotlib you are using. Older versions of Matplotlib handle 3D plotting differently.
